categories.label: No variation needed
categories.rule: No submission: the change is managed under the quality system (or an approved protocol).

categories.label: Separate procedure (not a variation)
categories.rule: Use the procedure named in the result (for example a transfer or an Article 61(3) notification).

categories.label: Type IA
categories.rule: Implement, then notify within 12 months (for example in the Type IA annual update). The authority checks it within 30 days.

categories.label: Type IA-IN
categories.rule: Implement, then notify immediately. The authority checks it within 30 days.

categories.label: Type IB
categories.rule: Notify before implementing; if the authority raises no objection within 30 days of a valid notification, the change is accepted.

categories.label: Type II
categories.rule: Implement only after approval: quality-only changes once the opinion or outcome is received; changes to the product information once the decision is amended.

categories.label: Extension application
categories.rule: An extension is assessed like a new application and needs a decision before marketing.

Q.II.b.1:1.text: The site was satisfactorily inspected in the last three years by an EU/EEA authority or an authority with a GMP mutual recognition agreement with the EU.

Q.II.b.1:2.text: The site is appropriately authorised for the pharmaceutical form or product concerned.

Q.II.b.1:4.text: Where relevant, a validation scheme is in place, or validation at the new site was done on at least three production-scale batches.

Q.II.b.2:4.text: Method transfer to the new site or laboratory is complete.

Q.II.b.2:5.text: At least one testing site stays in the EU/EEA or in a country with a suitable GMP agreement.

Q.II.b.3:1.text: No change in the qualitative or quantitative impurity profile or in physicochemical properties.

Q.II.b.3:2.text: The product is an immediate-release oral form or a non-sterile solution, or the change is to a non-critical parameter already assessed as having no quality impact.

Q.II.b.3:3.text: The manufacturing principle and individual steps stay the same, with no change of solvents.

Q.II.b.3:4.text: The process stays under the existing in-process controls, with no widened or deleted limits.

Q.II.b.3:5.text: Finished product and intermediate specifications are unchanged.

Q.II.b.3:6.text: The new process gives a product identical in quality, safety and efficacy.

Q.II.b.3:7.text: Stability studies have started on at least one pilot or industrial batch, with a commitment to finish them.

Q.II.b.3:8.text: The change does not come from unexpected manufacturing events, stability concerns or a safety or quality issue.

Q.II.b.4:1.text: Reproducibility and consistency of the product are unaffected.

Q.II.b.4:2.text: The product is an immediate-release oral form or a non-sterile solution.

Q.II.b.4:3.text: Method and in-process control changes are only those the new size needs.

Q.II.b.4:4.text: A validation scheme is in place, or validation was done on at least three batches at the new size.

Q.II.b.4:5.text: The product is not a biological product.

Q.II.b.4:6.text: The change does not come from unexpected manufacturing events or stability concerns.

Q.II.b.4:7.text: The new size is within ten times the size foreseen at approval (or after a later change not made as Type IA).

Q.II.b.5:1.text: The change does not follow from an earlier commitment to review the in-process control.

Q.II.b.5:2.text: The change does not come from unexpected manufacturing events, stability concerns or a safety or quality issue.

Q.II.b.5:5.text: A new analytical procedure is not a novel technique or a standard technique used in a novel way.

Q.II.b.5:7.text: The control does not cover a critical attribute (assay, purity, impurities, critical physical characteristics, identity, required microbiological controls).

Q.II.b.5:9.text: The change is not part of a control strategy revision aimed at reducing testing.

Q.II.b.5(f):2.text: The change does not come from unexpected manufacturing events or a safety or quality issue.

Q.II.b.5(f):4.text: The analytical procedure stays the same or changes only in minor ways (no different column type or method).

Q.II.b.5(f):6.text: The procedure is not biological, immunological or immunochemical.

Q.II.b.5(f):8.text: Studies show the updated procedure is at least equivalent to the former one.

Q.I.a.1:1.text: Specifications, in-process controls, method of preparation (including batch size) and route of synthesis are the same as approved.

Q.I.a.1:2.text: The active substance is neither biological nor sterile.

Q.I.a.1:3.text: No new supplier of materials of human or animal origin needing viral safety or TSE assessment.

Q.I.a.2:1.text: No adverse change in the impurity profile or physicochemical properties.

Q.I.a.2:2.text: Same route, intermediates, reagents, catalysts and solvents (for biologics: same steps, parameters, controls and specifications).

Q.I.a.2:3.text: Active substance and intermediate specifications are unchanged.

Q.I.a.2:5.text: The change does not come from unexpected manufacturing events, stability issues or a safety or quality problem.

Q.I.b.2:1.text: Validation shows the updated procedure is at least equivalent to the former one.

Q.I.b.2:2.text: Total impurity limits are unchanged and no new unqualified impurities are found.

Q.I.b.2:4.text: The change is fully described in the open part of the ASMF, if there is one.

Q.II.a.1:1.text: Release and end-of-shelf-life specifications are unchanged apart from appearance.

Q.II.a.1:2.text: Any ink meets the relevant pharmaceutical rules.

Q.II.a.1:4.text: Markings that tell strengths apart are not removed.

Q.II.a.3:1.text: Functional characteristics of the dosage form (disintegration, dissolution) are unchanged.

Q.II.a.3:2.text: Any weight adjustment uses an excipient that is already a major part of the formulation.

Q.II.a.3:3.text: The finished product specification changes only for appearance, odour or taste (and removal of an identification test if relevant).

Q.II.a.3:4.text: ICH stability studies have started on at least two pilot or industrial batches, with at least three months of satisfactory data at implementation.

Q.II.a.3:5.text: New components comply with EU food additive and flavouring rules.

Q.II.a.3:6.text: No new components of human or animal origin needing viral safety or TSE data.

Q.II.a.3:7.text: Strength differentiation is unaffected and paediatric taste acceptability is not made worse.

Q.II.a.3:8.text: Dissolution of the new product on at least two pilot batches is comparable to the old one.

Q.II.a.3:9.text: The change does not come from stability problems and raises no safety concern.

Q.II.a.3:10.text: The product is not a biological product.

Q.II.d.1:1.text: The change does not come from an earlier commitment to review acceptance criteria.

Q.II.d.1:2.text: The change does not come from unexpected manufacturing events, stability concerns or a safety or quality issue.

Q.II.d.1:3.text: The change is not part of a control strategy revision aimed at reducing testing.

Q.II.d.1:5.text: A new analytical procedure is not a novel technique or a standard technique used in a novel way.

Q.II.d.1:6.text: The change does not involve impurities (including genotoxic ones) or dissolution.

Q.II.d.1:7.text: The attribute is not critical (identity, assay, purity, impurities, critical physical characteristics, tests required by the Ph. Eur. for the dosage form).

Q.II.d.2:1.text: Validation shows the updated procedure is at least equivalent to the former one.

Q.II.d.2:2.text: Total impurity limits are unchanged and no new unqualified impurities are found.

Q.II.d.2:3.text: The method of analysis stays the same (parameters such as column length or temperature only).

Q.II.d.2:4.text: An alternative analytical procedure is already authorised for the attribute.

Q.II.e.1:1.text: The change involves the same container type only (for example blister to blister).

Q.II.e.1:2.text: The proposed material is at least equivalent to the approved one in the relevant properties.

Q.II.e.1:3.text: ICH stability studies have started on at least two pilot or industrial batches, with at least three months of data at implementation (not needed for a more protective pack).

Q.II.e.1:5.text: The product is not a biological product.

Q.II.e.2:1.text: No change to the qualitative or quantitative composition of the container.

Q.II.e.2:2.text: The change does not affect a fundamental part of the packaging that affects delivery, use, safety or stability.

Q.II.e.2:3.text: If headspace or surface-to-volume ratio changes, stability studies have started with at least three months of data.

Q.II.e.3:1.text: The change does not involve a part of the packaging that affects delivery, use, safety or stability.

Q.II.e.6:1.text: The new pack size fits the posology and treatment duration in the SmPC.

Q.II.e.6:2.text: The immediate packaging material is unchanged.

Q.II.e.8:1.text: The secondary packaging has no functional stability role, or the new one is not less protective.

Q.II.e.8:2.text: The changed component suits storage at the authorised conditions.

Q.II.e.8:3.text: The change is not due to critical deficiencies of the former component.

Q.II.e.8:4.text: The change does not result from unexpected events during manufacture or storage.

Q.II.f.1:1.text: The change does not come from unexpected manufacturing events or stability concerns.

Q.II.f.1:2.text: No widening of acceptance criteria, no removal of stability-indicating parameters and no reduced testing frequency.

Q.II.f.1:3.text: Studies follow the approved protocol, real-time data are submitted, all batches meet specification at all time points, with no unexpected trends.

Q.II.f.1:4.text: The product is not a biological or herbal product.

Q.II.f.1:5.text: The product is an immediate-release film-coated tablet.

Q.II.f.1:6.text: The product is not on the Union list of critical medicines (or a similar national list).

Q.II.g.5:1.text: The change was made fully in line with the PACMP, and its acceptance criteria are met.

E.4:1.text: The holder remains the same legal entity.

Q.I.a.3:1.text: Any change to the manufacturing method is only what scale-up or downscaling needs (for example equipment size).

Q.I.a.3:2.text: Results of at least two batches at the proposed size meet the specification.

Q.I.a.3:3.text: The active substance is not a biological substance.

Q.I.a.3:4.text: The change does not adversely affect the reproducibility of the process.

Q.I.a.3:5.text: The change is fully described in the open part of the ASMF, if there is one.

Q.I.a.3:6.text: Active substance and intermediate specifications stay the same, and the impurity control strategy remains appropriate.

Q.I.a.3:7.text: The active substance is not sterile.

Q.I.a.3:8.text: The change does not come from unexpected events during manufacture or from stability concerns.

Q.I.d.1:1.text: The change does not come from unexpected events during manufacture or from stability concerns.

Q.I.d.1:2.text: Studies follow the approved protocol, real-time data are submitted, all batches meet the specification and no unexpected trends appear.

Q.I.d.1:3.text: The physical state of the active substance is unchanged.

Q.II.a.2:1.text: Dissolution of the new product is comparable to the old one (disintegration for herbal products).

Q.II.a.2:2.text: Release and end-of-shelf-life specifications are unchanged apart from shape or dimensions.

Q.II.a.2:3.text: Qualitative and quantitative composition and mean mass are unchanged.

Q.II.a.2:4.text: It is not a scored tablet intended to divide into equal doses.

Q.II.a.4:1.text: Dissolution of two batches is comparable to the old product (disintegration for herbal products).

Q.II.a.4:2.text: The coating or shell is not critical for release or other attributes.

Q.II.a.4:3.text: The finished product specification changes only for weight and dimensions.

Q.II.a.4:4.text: Stability studies have started on at least two pilot or industrial batches, with at least three months of data.

Q.II.b.2:1.text: The batch release manufacturer is in the EU/EEA with a valid manufacturing authorisation, and one release site stays in the EU/EEA.

Q.II.b.2:3.text: The analytical procedure is not biological, immunological or immunochemical.

Q.II.b.5:3.text: Any change is within the range of the currently approved limits.

Q.II.b.5:4.text: The analytical procedure stays the same, or changes only in minor ways.

Q.II.b.5:6.text: The analytical procedure is not biological, immunological or immunochemical.

Q.II.b.5:8.text: Studies in line with the relevant guidelines show the updated procedure is at least equivalent to the former one.

Q.II.c.1:1.text: The change does not come from an earlier commitment to review acceptance criteria.

Q.II.c.1:2.text: The change does not come from unexpected events during manufacture or from stability concerns.

Q.II.c.1:3.text: The change is not part of a control strategy revision aimed at reducing redundant testing.

Q.II.c.1:4.text: The analytical procedure stays the same, or changes only in minor ways.

Q.II.c.1:5.text: A new analytical procedure is not a novel non-standard technique or a standard technique used in a novel way.

Q.II.c.1:6.text: The change does not concern a genotoxic impurity.

Q.II.c.1:7.text: The attribute does not control a critical attribute of the excipient.

Q.II.c.3:1.text: Excipient and finished product release and shelf-life specifications are unchanged.

Q.II.e.7:2.text: The composition and design specifications of the component stay the same.

Q.II.e.7:3.text: Specifications and quality control procedures are at least equivalent.

Q.II.e.7:4.text: Any sterilisation method and conditions stay the same.

Q.II.g.3:1.text: The deletion does not come from unexpected events or out-of-specification results during implementation and does not affect approved dossier information.

Q.III.1:1.text: The impact of the new source is evaluated: no change to critical quality attributes or composition, and release and shelf-life specifications are unchanged.

Q.III.1:2.text: Active substance impurity specifications are unchanged (tightening is allowed).

Q.III.1:3.text: Other relevant properties (for example polymorph, hydration state, particle size) are unchanged.

Q.III.1:4.text: No material of human or animal origin needing viral safety data is used in the process.

Q.III.1:5.text: The active substance is tested before use if the CEP has no re-test period and the dossier lacks supporting data.

Q.III.1:9.text: For a non-sterile active substance used in a sterile product, no water is used in the last synthesis steps, or the water guideline is met.

Q.IV.1:1.text: No significant impact on delivery, quality, safety, efficacy or usability.

Q.IV.1:3.text: No substantial amendment of the product information is needed.

Q.IV.1:5.text: There is no impact on the risk management plan.

E.1:1.text: EMA has finished its check of the new name, with a positive result.

E.2:1.text: The substance, excipient, device part or component itself is unchanged.

E.4:2.text: The physical location of the site and all manufacturing operations stay the same.

E.5:1.text: At least one authorised site with the same function remains (with a release site able to certify in the EU/EEA, where relevant).

E.5:2.text: The deletion is not due to critical manufacturing deficiencies.

multipleChanges.rule: A group follows the procedure of its highest variation type. Groups are allowed for related changes in the cases of Annex III, or when the authority agrees.

IA.label: Notify within 12 months of implementation (annual update)

IB.label: Accepted if no objection within 30 days of a valid notification

II.label: Standard 60-day evaluation (90 days for indication changes, 30 for some safety changes), plus clock stops

EXT.label: Assessed like an initial application: 210 days plus clock stops, then the decision

variation.label: Cover letter listing the variations, their classification and the procedure
Variation application form (eAF), with the present/proposed table and the declaration of conditions met

pi.label: Product information (SmPC, labelling, package leaflet), clean and with changes highlighted

other.label: Cover letter or notification for the procedure named in the result

changeLog.text: First EU edition: 73 changes classified with the Commission guidelines C/2025/5045 (applying from 15 January 2026), with the annex conditions as checklists, grouping, the Type IA annual update, worksharing and super-grouping.
